clue.text: Neglected pro couldn’t please the judges more

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, the same as for
read as GOT TEN: a perfect ten from the judges is the top score, so nothing could please them more

explanation.surface: A professional performer has been overlooked despite earning top marks from the judging panel.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer FOR GOT TEN: a ten is the maximum mark in scoring sports like gymnastics or ice dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left out of mind and ignored has slipped from memory, hence passed over and uncared for.

clue.text: Extremely supportive of love letter

indicators.note: in a down clue a word that supports another sits underneath it, so this piece goes below the other

blocks.note: love is a zero score in tennis, shaped like the letter O
mega is slang for extremely, as in mega rich

explanation.surface: Someone is enthusiastically backing a love letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final character of the Greek alphabet, so it is a letter in that script.

clue.text: Withdraw research discipline

blocks.note: to go into a subject is to research or investigate it
a hiding is a beating, a harsh form of discipline

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out of an academic field of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Research discipline' reads as one academic subject, but it splits into a verb and a noun meaning a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Concealing yourself away from others is a way of retreating from public view and contact.

clue.text: Pictures a large-scale 22 Down?

definitions.note: cryptic: a hiding place on a grand scale

blocks.note: first meaning: the cinema, as in going to the pictures
second meaning, cryptic: 22 Down is a hiding, and a ... hides things, so a huge one is a hiding place writ large

explanation.walkthrough: 22 Down is HIDING. A screen is something to hide behind, so a big screen is a large-scale way of hiding; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the pictures means visiting the cinema, which is often called by its giant projection surface.

clue.text: Dadaist back on cycle

indicators.note: going round a cycle moves letters from the front of the word round to its end

blocks.note: the stern is the back end of a ship

explanation.surface: An avant-garde artist is back on his bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like returning, but it is the rear of a boat; 'on cycle' moves its opening pair of letters round to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst, the German painter, was a leading figure of the Dada movement before turning to Surrealism.

clue.text: In liquor, core of revellers cools off – here?

definitions.text: In liquor, core of revellers cools off – here?

indicators.note: in places what follows inside the drink, so those letters are enclosed
the core of a word is its very centre, so only the middle letter is wanted

blocks.note: a potation is an alcoholic drink, the first part before the insertion
the fifth of nine letters is the centre
ices means cools, chills

explanation.surface: Where does a drunken partygoer sleep it off? The clue answers itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a reveller who has had too much liquor may be locked up to cool off in a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Drunk and disorderly revellers are taken to the local police headquarters to sober up in the cells overnight.

clue.text: American critic rubbished Dragon Pale Ale

indicators.note: something rubbished is trashed and torn apart, so the letters are broken up and reformed

blocks.note: the three words of the beer's name supply the letters

explanation.surface: A reviewer pans a pale ale brewed under a Dragon label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Critic' and 'rubbished' make a natural pair in the surface, but the critic is the definition and only 'rubbished' acts on the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe was famous for tales and poems, but he also earned his living as a sharp literary reviewer.

clue.text: See 9
D’oh! No, I’m not me – verse seems shaky

definitions.text: D’oh! No, I’m not me – verse seems shaky

indicators.note: shaky words are unsteady and wobble out of place, so their letters are rearranged

blocks.clueFragment: D’oh! No, I’m not me – verse seems
blocks.note: every letter before the signal word is used

explanation.surface: Homer Simpson's catchphrase, then a writer admitting he is off form and his poetry is wobbly.
explanation.walkthrough: D'oh is Homer Simpson's cry, but the whole clue also describes the epic poet Homer having an off day with his verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says that even the greatest masters, like the poet of the Iliad, occasionally make mistakes or lapse.

clue.text: See 27
See instrument with bits flipped over

indicators.note: flipping over a small part turns that part round to face the other way

blocks.note: the viola is a stringed instrument slightly larger than a violin

explanation.surface: Look at a musical instrument whose parts have been turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle two letters IO are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Voila is a French exclamation meaning there it is, used like look or behold when revealing something.

clue.text: Time to get a train

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
a in the sense of per, as in a pound a head

explanation.surface: It's time to catch a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway train, but it is the verb meaning to instruct.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct or coach someone in a skill is to educate them, the verbal sense of train.

clue.text: Bribed retiring head of TSB branch

indicators.note: someone retiring leaves the scene, so a letter departs from the word
the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a bribed official has been bought
the opening letter of the bank's initials

explanation.surface: A corrupt manager of a TSB bank branch is retiring; TSB is a British high-street bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branch' looks like a bank branch, but it is the tree sense. BOUGHT loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A large limb growing from a tree trunk is a bough, so it is a main tree branch.

clue.text: Get ready to attack

blocks.note: first meaning, split 2,3
second meaning: to assail on all sides

explanation.surface: Someone is told to prepare for an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction, but it is two definitions joined by 'to'; the first splits as BE SET.
explanation.definitionFit: To beset is to harass or assail persistently, as troubles or enemies surround and harry someone.

clue.text: Wee bully you shouldn’t have let off

indicators.note: something let off is released and allowed to go, so those letters drop away

blocks.note: bully read as bull-like; taurine means relating to a bull
what you say when given a present, a thank-you; ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A small schoolyard bully who should not have been released without punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like small, but it is the noun. TAURINE loses TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Wee is a childish and informal British word for the liquid passed when you go to the toilet.

clue.text: Comedy duo splitting with ace tennis star

indicators.note: a duo splitting with a partner parts company, so that partner leaves

blocks.note: Hale and Pace were a British comedy double act on television
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedy double act breaks up after a falling out with a top tennis player.
explanation.walkthrough: Ace looks like a tennis serve to go with the star, but it is the three letters taken from PACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Simona Halep is a Romanian former world number one who won Wimbledon and the French Open.

clue.text: Pointer essential after having been cut off round lake

indicators.note: cutting off a word chops away its tail end
round says the shortened word wraps around the next piece

blocks.note: essential things are needed
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A sign pointing to something essential has been cut off by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: NEEDED loses its last D, then NEEDE is wrapped round L.
explanation.definitionFit: The needle on a dial or compass is the thin indicator that points to a reading or direction.

clue.text: Media targets put weight on broadcast

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece placed on another is attached after it

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial broadcast
mass is a measure of weight

explanation.surface: Advertisers aiming at their audiences put weight on a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Admass is the section of the public easily swayed by advertising and mass marketing, the audience that adverts aim at.

clue.text: Spirits coming from here yet?

blocks.note: first meaning: the distilling apparatus that produces whisky or gin
second meaning: up to now, even now

explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as asking whether ghosts have arrived; spirits are actually liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: A distillery apparatus that makes liquor shares its name with the adverb meaning even now or up to this time.

clue.text: Dull-witted oaf’s left tubes out of shape

indicators.note: the left-hand end of a word is its first letter
pushed out of shape, the letters lose their order and are rearranged

blocks.note: the leftmost letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clumsy oaf has left some tubes bent and misshapen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as abandoned, but it picks the leftmost letter of oaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse describes someone slow to understand, so it means stupid or slow on the uptake.

clue.text: "Where’s Roma?" I’ll go for Spain (and others)

indicators.note: one thing going for another takes its place

blocks.note: Roma is the Italian name of Rome, and Italia the native name of its country
I will: the subject I is the letter to be replaced
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Someone asks where Rome is and offers to try Spain instead, along with other places.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening I of ITALIA is swapped for E.
explanation.definitionFit: Et alia is Latin for and other things or people, the full form of the abbreviation et al.

clue.text: Important info for better actor

blocks.note: the, stressed as 'thee', marks the pre-eminent one, as in the place to be
SP is the starting price, the odds a bettor on horse racing needs

explanation.surface: Someone passes on vital information to a gambler, then names a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective, but it is someone who bets; split the answer 3,2.
explanation.definitionFit: Thesp is an informal, slightly jokey shortening of thespian, a theatrical performer.

clue.text: See 3
See 4
Legal bar trainees to prosecute cases

definitions.note: read as the verb phrase to bar legally

indicators.note: the words act as a case or casing that holds the letters inside them

blocks.note: the end of the first word, all of the second, and the opening of the third

explanation.surface: Junior barristers being trained to prosecute legal cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legal bar' looks like the profession of barristers, but it means to bar legally.
explanation.definitionFit: To estop is to prevent someone in law from asserting something contrary to their earlier statements.

clue.text: Is this schoolboy error about to blow classroom’s centrepiece ...

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read back to front
to blow something is to lose or squander it, so a letter is lost
the centrepiece of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: a slip-up is a mistake
the fifth of nine letters is the centre

explanation.surface: A boy's classroom mistake is about to wreck the room's central display; the dots lead into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIPUP is turned round to PUPILS, which then loses its last S.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolboy is a child being taught at school, which is what a pupil is.

clue.text: Slowly complied with 50 per cent of Polonius’s advice?

definitions.text: complied with 50 per cent of Polonius’s advice?

blocks.note: first meaning: a musical tempo marking

blocks.clueFragment: complied with 50 per cent of Polonius’s advice?
blocks.note: second meaning, cryptic: split 4,1 as lent nothing, so obeying 'nor a lender be' but not necessarily the borrower half

explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet, Polonius tells his son 'Neither a borrower nor a lender be'. Someone who LENT 0 (zero) kept only the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is an Italian tempo direction in music telling performers to play at a slow pace.

clue.text: ... as gymnast put match to dynamite?

blocks.note: putting a match to something sets it alight
HE stands for high explosive, and dynamite is one

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the schoolboy's blunder is like a gymnast lighting explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join it to the schoolboy clue above, but this clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnasts are supple and agile, which is what being lithe describes.

clue.text: This time’s best tournament limit: easy to split people here when running

indicators.note: something that splits another goes between its letters, breaking it in two

blocks.note: comp is short for competition
a limen is a threshold, a limit of perception
these people, the ones present
a soft option is an easy one
as in the sense of while
a show that is running is on

explanation.surface: A race organiser says this year's top event has a limit so runners can spread out.
explanation.walkthrough: Limen, a threshold, is mainly a psychology word. 'Easy' splits the people here after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a festive greeting at Christmas, offering good wishes for this time of year.

clue.text: Guarding rocker, one who clocks party promoter?

indicators.note: guarding something means surrounding it protectively, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: to clock is to notice or see, so one who does is a seer
a logan or logan stone is a large balanced rocking stone

explanation.surface: A bouncer protecting a rock musician spots someone promoting a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocker' looks like a musician, but a logan is a rocking stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A political party relies on someone coining catchy slogans to promote its message, hence the playful question mark.
